spec: Validate a relative file path string using '/' as the separator. The path must be non-empty, must not start or end with '/', and each '/'-separated segment must be non-empty, must not be exactly '.' or '..', and must consist only of letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, or dots. Return False if any rule is violated.

Validate a general email address for spam-filtering purposes. It must contain exactly one '@' splitting it into a non-empty local part (letters, digits, dots, underscores, plus signs, or hyphens only) and a domain part that contains at least one dot and whose dot-separated labels are all non-empty and alphanumeric (hyphens allowed). Additionally, given a second argument `blocked_domains` (a list of domain strings), the email's domain (case-insensitively) must NOT be one of the blocked domains. Return True only if the address is well-formed AND not blocked.

Validate an IPv4 address string in dotted-quad notation. It must split by '.' into exactly 4 parts, each part consisting only of digits, representing a value from 0 to 255, and must not have a leading zero unless the part is exactly '0'. Return False if any rule is violated.

Validate a CIDR-notation IPv4 string of the form 'address/prefix'. The address portion must be a valid dotted-quad IPv4 address (4 dot-separated parts, each digits 0-255, no leading zeros unless the part is '0'). The prefix portion must be digits only, with no leading zero unless it is exactly '0', representing an integer from 0 to 32. The string must contain exactly one '/'.

Validate a full-form IPv6 address string (no '::' compression allowed). It must split by ':' into exactly 8 groups, each group a string of 1 to 4 hexadecimal digit characters (0-9, a-f, A-F). Return False otherwise.
Validate a MAC address string. It must consist of exactly 6 groups of exactly 2 hexadecimal digit characters (0-9, a-f, A-F), separated by colons. Return False otherwise.

Validate a MAC address string that uses hyphens as separators. It must consist of exactly 6 groups of exactly 2 hexadecimal digit characters (0-9, a-f, A-F), separated by hyphens. Return False otherwise.
Validate a full-form hex color string. It must start with '#' followed by exactly 6 hexadecimal digit characters (0-9, a-f, A-F), for a total length of 7. Return False otherwise.
Validate a shorthand hex color string. It must start with '#' followed by exactly 3 hexadecimal digit characters (0-9, a-f, A-F), for a total length of 4. Return False otherwise.

Validate a hex color string with an alpha channel. It must start with '#' followed by exactly 8 hexadecimal digit characters (0-9, a-f, A-F) representing red, green, blue and alpha components, for a total length of 9. Return False otherwise.

Validate a password against a basic policy: it must be at least 8 characters long and contain at least one uppercase letter, at least one lowercase letter, and at least one digit. Return False if any requirement is not met.

Validate a password against a strict policy: it must be at least 10 characters long, contain no whitespace characters, and include at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one special character from the set '!@#$%^&*'. Return False if any requirement is not met.

Given a password string and a username string, validate that the password is at least 8 characters long and does not contain the username as a case-insensitive substring anywhere within it. Return False if the password is too short or the username appears inside it.

Validate a password requiring all four character classes: it must be between 8 and 64 characters long (inclusive) and contain at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one special (non-alphanumeric) character. Return False if any requirement is not met.
Validate a password: it must contain no whitespace characters, be between 6 and 20 characters long (inclusive), and contain at least 2 digit characters. Return False if any requirement is not met.

Validate a password: it must be at least 8 characters long and contain at least 3 of the following 4 character classes: lowercase letters, uppercase letters, digits, and special (non-alphanumeric) characters. Return False if fewer than 3 classes are present or the password is too short.

Given a candidate password string and a list of common passwords, validate that the password is at least 8 characters long and is not equal (case-insensitively) to any password in the common list. Return False if the password is too short or matches a common password.
Validate a password: it must be between 8 and 32 characters long (inclusive) and must not contain any whitespace character (space, tab, newline, etc.). Return False otherwise.

Validate that a string does not contain a run of 3 or more consecutive characters whose Unicode code points are strictly ascending by exactly 1 each step (like 'abc' or '123'). Scan left to right tracking the current ascending run length; if it reaches 3, return False. An empty string, or one with no such run, returns True.

Validate a time string in the 24-hour format 'HH:MM:SS' with each field zero-padded to 2 digits. Hours must be 00-23, minutes 00-59, seconds 00-59. Return False for any malformed or out-of-range time.
Validate a time string in the short 24-hour format 'HH:MM' with each field zero-padded to 2 digits. Hours must be 00-23 and minutes must be 00-59. Return False for any malformed or out-of-range time.

Validate a combined date-time string in the simplified ISO format 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS' (a literal 'T' separates the date from the time). The date portion must be a valid calendar date (accounting for leap years) and the time portion must have hours 00-23, minutes 00-59, seconds 00-59, each field with the required zero-padded width. Return False for any malformed or out-of-range value.

Given two date strings `start` and `end`, each in ISO format 'YYYY-MM-DD', validate that both are well-formed valid calendar dates (accounting for leap years) AND that `start` is not later than `end` (chronologically). Return False if either string is not a valid date or if start comes after end.

Validate a duration string composed of optional hour, minute and second components in that fixed order, each written as a non-negative integer (no leading zeros unless the value is exactly '0') immediately followed by its unit letter 'h', 'm', or 's' (e.g. '1h30m', '45m', '2h30m15s', '10s'). At least one component must be present, no other characters or whitespace are allowed, and a unit must not be repeated or appear out of order. Return False if the string violates any of these rules.

Validate a US-style date string in the format 'MM/DD/YYYY' (2-digit zero-padded month, 2-digit zero-padded day, 4-digit year, slash-separated). The month must be 01-12 and the day must be valid for that month and year, correctly accounting for leap years. Return False for any malformed or out-of-range date.

Validate a year-month string in the format 'YYYY-MM' (4-digit year, 2-digit zero-padded month, dash-separated). The month must be between 01 and 12 inclusive. Return False for any malformed or out-of-range value.

Given an integer n, determine whether it is a numeric palindrome: its decimal string representation (without a sign) reads the same forwards and backwards. Negative numbers are never palindromes (return False for any n < 0).

Given a string of lowercase letters, determine whether some permutation (reordering) of its characters could form a palindrome. This is possible exactly when at most one character has an odd count of occurrences. Return True if a palindrome permutation is possible, otherwise False. An empty string is considered valid (True).

Given a string of lowercase letters, determine whether it can become a palindrome by removing at most one character. Return True if the string is already a palindrome, or becomes one after deleting exactly one character (checked by a standard two-pointer approach with a single allowed mismatch skip), otherwise False.

Validate a card display format string: it must consist of exactly 4 space-separated groups, and each group must be either exactly 4 digit characters or exactly 4 uppercase 'X' characters (used to mask a group). Return False if the format, group count, or group content is invalid.

Validate a bank account masking string: it must start with exactly 4 asterisk characters '****' followed by between 4 and 12 digit characters (inclusive), representing the visible trailing portion of a masked account number. The total length is therefore between 8 and 16 characters. Return False otherwise.

Validate a string as a legal Python-style identifier: it must be non-empty, its first character must be a letter or underscore, every character must be a letter, digit, or underscore, and it must not be one of the reserved keywords {'if','else','elif','for','while','def','return','class','import','in','not','and','or','True','False','None','break','continue','pass','try','except','finally','with','as','lambda','yield'}. Return False otherwise.
Validate an octal string: it must be non-empty and consist only of the digit characters '0' through '7'. Return False if it is empty or contains any other character (including '8' or '9').

Validate a Base64-encoded string format: the length must be a positive multiple of 4, at most the last 2 characters may be '=' padding characters (occurring only at the very end), and every non-padding character must be a letter (upper or lower case), digit, '+', or '/'. Return False otherwise.

Validate a simplified variable declaration string of the form 'type name' (a type keyword, one space, then an identifier). The type must be exactly one of 'int', 'float', 'str', 'bool'. The name must be non-empty, start with a letter or underscore, and consist only of letters, digits, and underscores. Return False otherwise.

Validate a camelCase identifier string: it must be non-empty, its first character must be a lowercase letter, and every character in the string must be alphanumeric (no underscores, hyphens, or other punctuation). Return False otherwise.

Validate a snake_case identifier string: it must be non-empty, its first character must be a lowercase letter, every character must be a lowercase letter, digit, or underscore, it must not end with an underscore, and it must not contain two consecutive underscores. Return False otherwise.
Validate a US ZIP code string: it must be either exactly 5 digit characters, or a ZIP+4 format of exactly 5 digits, a hyphen, and 4 more digits. Return False otherwise.
Validate a Canadian postal code string in the format 'A1A 1A1': uppercase letter, digit, uppercase letter, space, digit, uppercase letter, digit. Return False if the pattern does not match exactly.

Validate a simplified UK-style postcode string: it must split into two parts on a single space, an outward code of 2 to 4 alphanumeric characters starting with a letter, and an inward code of exactly 3 characters: a digit followed by two letters. Return False otherwise.
